2026-11-12.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-11-12.name: Saint Theodore the Studite
2026-11-12.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Saint Theodore the Studite on November 12. Born in 759 in Constantinople, Theodore became a monk and later abbot of the Stoudios Monastery, leading a renewal of common prayer, work and learning. He defended the veneration of icons when emperors attacked it and endured exile more than once rather than yield; his letters and teachings guided monks, families and leaders across the Byzantine world.
2026-11-12.provenance: Brief story based on Wikipedia. The date follows the Maronite calendar.

2026-11-13.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-11-13.name: Saint John Chrysostom
2026-11-13.story: The Maronite calendar honors Saint John Chrysostom on November 13. Born around 347 in Antioch and raised by his widowed mother Anthusa, John became a priest whose preaching was so clear and fervent that people called him golden-mouthed - Chrysostom. As archbishop of Constantinople he spoke for the poor and called the Church to conversion, which cost him exile; the Divine Liturgy prayed around the world still carries his name, and the Church honors him as a Doctor.
2026-11-13.provenance: Brief story based on the Orthodox Church in America. The date follows the Maronite calendar.
2026-11-13.sourceLabel: Feast source: Eparchy of St. Maron liturgical calendar

2026-11-14.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-11-14.name: Saint Philip the Apostle
2026-11-14.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Saint Philip the Apostle on November 14. Philip came from Bethsaida in Galilee, the town of Peter and Andrew. When Jesus called him with the words "Follow me," Philip's first response was to find Nathanael and bring him to Christ with the invitation "Come and see" (John 1:43-46). One of the Twelve, he is remembered in tradition as a tireless preacher of the Gospel.

2026-11-15.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-11-15.calendar: Maronite commemoration; Sunday of the Announcement to Zechariah
2026-11-15.name: Saints Gurias, Samonas and Habib
2026-11-15.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Saints Gurias, Samonas and Habib on November 15. Gurias and Samonas were Christians of Edessa who refused to abandon their faith during persecution. Habib, a deacon of the same city, bore witness to Christ in a later persecution. The Church remembers these martyrs together for their steadfast faith.
2026-11-15.provenance: Brief account based on Orthodox Church in America. The date follows the Maronite calendar. This date is also the Sunday of the Announcement to Zechariah.

2026-11-16.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-11-16.name: Saint Matthew the Evangelist
2026-11-16.story: The Maronite calendar honors Saint Matthew the Evangelist on November 16. The Gospel tells how Jesus called Matthew from his work as a tax collector, and Matthew rose and followed him. One of the Twelve Apostles, he is traditionally associated with the first Gospel. His call reminds Christians that the mercy of Christ opens the way to a new life.

2026-11-17.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-11-17.name: Saint Gregory the Wonderworker
2026-11-17.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Saint Gregory the Wonderworker on November 17. Born into a non-Christian family, Gregory encountered the Christian teacher Origen, studied with him and received baptism. He later became bishop of Neocaesarea, preaching the Gospel and guiding his community through persecution. The title Wonderworker reflects the miracles attributed to him in Christian tradition.

2026-11-18.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-11-18.name: Saint Romanos the Martyr
2026-11-18.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Saint Romanos on November 18. A deacon from Caesarea in Palestine, Romanos was living in Antioch when Christians faced persecution. He encouraged the faithful to remain steadfast and publicly confessed his faith in Christ. Arrested and imprisoned, he suffered martyrdom rather than deny that faith.

2026-11-19.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-11-19.name: Pope Saint Pontian
2026-11-19.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Pope Saint Pontian on November 19. Pontian led the Church of Rome from the year 230. During persecution he was exiled to Sardinia, where he resigned his office. He died in exile in 235 and was honored in Rome as a martyr.
2026-11-19.provenance: Brief account based on Vatican News (Spanish). The date follows the Maronite calendar.
